reconstruction.scope: Würzburg Residence complete connected palace exterior on its actual relation outline: open western Ehrenhof and four fully open mapped inner courtyards; long sandstone garden range with central taller pavilion, steep slate roofs and two curved outer roof masses, western wing-end pediments, repeated three-level glazing/cornices, triple western and garden entrances, physical front columns and recessed side colonnades. Low dormers, balustrades, restrained original abstract roof figures and small verdigris turret carry the photographed identity. Gardens/fountain, separate town buildings and interiors remain outside this building model. No copied sculpture, frescoes, text or interior decoration.

reconstruction.heightBasis: Three ordinary front/aerial pictures guide medium-fi exterior. Mapped23m height is an approximate envelope, not surveyed levels. Working lower walls18m with slate hips to24m, curved outer roofs to29m and central garden pavilion walls22m/roof29.5m plus original abstract crown to32m, above+.2m floor. Three-level facade rhythm, roof subdivisions/dormers, colonnade counts, curved roof profiles, ornaments and small turret are approximations. No copied statues, coats of arms, frescoes, inscriptions, furnished rooms or fountain/garden sculpture.
reconstruction.terrainBasis: Qualified approximate native palace exterior fit on original Protomaps20261020/Mapzen201x201/6m ground. Open Ehrenhof provider[0,10] supplies188.94774001662032m datum. Boundary grades-2.798..+.482m; floor+.2m and foundation-2.978m provide supported bases with up to about3m of low-side plinth exposure and modest high-side burial. Four actual court holes and open forecourt retain original terrain; their exact historic paving/levels remain approximate. A closed raised western apron supports four front columns and thresholds; recessed side colonnades retain original adjoining ground. Four hole-free occupied partitions plus apron mask remove only palace contact ground. All independent town buildings, garden approaches, roads and water remain intact. Native views establish approximate contact; flat review planes partly bury grade-specific bases. No bespoke terrain/survey or flattening; exact thresholds and accessibility unverified.
